dialogues.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
dialogues.text: Hello, my rising graffiti stars. Anything else you'd like to know?

dialogues.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
dialogues.text: If there's nothing else, get ready to head out! I'll be out for a walk through the wilds myself. Gotta look for good cliffsides that haven't been painted yet. Don't you be slower than me, now!

choices.text: Tell me about graffiti as an art form...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm. It's all over Natlan in crazy colors — on houses, trees, mountains, even on people...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It seems to be a custom here, so... when did it start?

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Aha, interested in hearing some graffiti history, are you? Good, good!

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: The techniques we ordinary people now master are generalized forms of "Phlogiston Engravings."

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: You might have heard of the process itself, where professional inscribers use blades to carve such engravings for mighty tribal warriors.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Each tribe has an engraving unique to them, and they are immensely useful, whether for communicating with Saurian companions, or in battle.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, that does ring a bell... So that's what it's called.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's no ordinary body of symbols...

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Indeed! For us normal folks, these symbols are marks of courage, ability, and honor. Nothing more avant-garde than these, if you ask me!

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: That's why many imitate the inscribers and spray similar patterns in various locations.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Of course, they're mighty champions, and we're pretty mundane by comparison, so our works don't serve much purpose beyond expressing our emotions.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Over time, the artistic content expanded from those patterns into all manner of different expressions, growing increasingly free-spirited, eventually evolving into its modern form.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Symbols of the strong, huh? That kinda makes sense... Who'd have thought graffiti had such a long history...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You know, we could pick a few large buildings in the Serenitea Pot and cover their walls in huge pictures of all the formidable people we've met during our journey!

choices.text: Haha, then let's start with that bard!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That would work! Why don't we draw a bunch of kittens nearby, too?

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Haha, draw on. Draw 'em all, even!

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Once your skills mature, you can showcase all the companions and objects you want, no problem!

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: But before that, you need to understand the core philosophy behind graffiti, and you need practice.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course! But just you wait — we're quick learners and then some!

choices.text: Our well-traveled, knowledgeable consultant would make the perfect candidate too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, yeah. Just the thought of it puts Paimon at ease! ... Wait, but would Tubby ever dare take a nap again?

choices.text: How about a Statue of Her Excellency, the God of Thunder?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Should we paint her in a more majestic pose? Maybe raise a couple more Finches?

choices.text: What say you to Mahakusaladhamma, the Blessed One of Wisdom?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We should decorate the Realm Within with some extra pretty flowers and plants, then!

choices.text: Perhaps Fontaine's number-one star might be a good pick.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great idea — we'd need a super gorgeous open-air stage to go with it, and maybe some pretty lighting too...

choices.text: So, about avant-garde artistic thought...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You always have lots to say about "avant-garde." Did you have a teacher who particularly emphasized that?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Paimon guesses that you've never left Natlan before, so are there schools here that specialize in teaching art?

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: School? Never been anywhere like that.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: I'm speaking from experience here, combined with books I've read that adventurers brought in from beyond our lands — of course, it took me a long while to figure it out.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: If anything, I'm the one teaching others, no?

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: It just so happens that I plan on leaving a training area in the Graffiti Alliance headquarters...

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: If I manage to help you uncover your talent, I might as well handle any newcomers in future too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Headquarters? Paimon thought your Alliance also existed as a sort of identity. Y'know, like Genius Invokation TCG players.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Well, we do have the... lofty ambition of matching the Adventurers' Guild, so having a headquarters is a must, even if that means a bit of fundraising!

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Our current plans have us finishing it in short order, so if you get the chance, do drop by and hang out with us!

choices.text: So, about your name...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's been meaning to ask that too. Is "Dopey Dazzler" your real name?

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: As graffiti artists, our real names aren't anywhere near as important as our titles!

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Mine comes from a very, very, very awesome friend...

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: She said I have an uncanny ability to discover dazzling color combos, and others say that I get all dopey when blending paints... So I combined the two, and the rest is history!

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: We haven't had much opportunity to hang out since we first met, but that title has been a massive inspiration to me!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A nickname inspired by an awesome friend... Guess that makes sense...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But as for the word "dopey"... Eh, guess "avant-garde" doesn't involve being too concerned about the meaning of individual words.

choices.text: We'll continue our studies.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup. We'll continue our search for inspiration, just as you've taught us!

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Right on! Don't forget to use both your heart and your head! Let your imagination run wild!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Kachina, is that you?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}? Paimon? Huh, didn't expect to see you here!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Wait, are you here on some sort of super-awesome commission? Is it about the Spiritway over there?

choices.text: Our present commission is pretty awesome, yes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of which, the person who commissioned us is also from the Children of Echoes. Maybe you know each other...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You describe your encounter with "Dopey Dazzler," her views on graffiti, and her invitation for you to study avant-garde thought...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Oh, so that's who you met? I know her.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: She doesn't look like a big deal, quite like me, in fact. But if you get her talking, she can go on forever... If you hang out with her a bit more, you might see a... different side to Natlan, I guess?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Did you become friends after she invited you to draw graffiti with her as well?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Well, not really? We met by chance...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: That was a long time ago. I was buying fruit at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame with my parents, and there she was, sitting at the paint shop entrance, watching as Acat blended paints.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: She would sit there for half a day, almost, not moving a muscle, as though she could see something special in all those different colors.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: She was so focused at that moment. It was like she couldn't care less about anything except the paints! And so I thought she wouldn't notice me—

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Only for her to notice the color of my clothes as I passed, then start chatting with me about our favorite colors. It was like she'd become a different person!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, your clothes are pretty unique! Seems like the Dopey Dazzler's got a good eye for this kind of thing.

choices.text: A fine balance between vitality, simplicity, and innocence.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, that's right! Why didn't Paimon think about that... But yeah, you look just right!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But now you mention it, it sounds like the old Dopey Dazzler was quite different from the person we met. Guess she was... less good at making friends back then?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: She might just have been like I was, kinda bad at dealing with people. I mean, everyone's busy training for battle or practicing their dancing...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: By contrast, someone who focuses on painting might find it hard to make friends...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Still, I find people who have their own goals and work hard at them super cool!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: As I watched her study colors and graffiti so intently, I had the feeling... that she'd stick to her goal and follow it to the end — not all that different from a hero of legend, really!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Perhaps the lack of recognition from others means that the more serious she gets, the better she'll be in the future?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... kind of? Maybe?

choices.text: The details aren't important.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: After I met Dopey Dazzler, she invited me to do graffiti together with her, but... Don't get me wrong, I love those pretty patterns. I just don't think I have the talent to come up with anything interesting.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: She said it was alright, though. Said that her graffiti would record our tribe's famous warriors, and that if I couldn't draw anything good, I could at least become a good drawing.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: "And when the time comes, let me, a graffiti artist famed across Natlan, be the one to draw a picture of Kachina, the famous warrior..."

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: And boy, did she look dazzling when she was talking about that!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: ...Still, will I really ever become a warrior worth my salt? Not that I told her so, though. Didn't want to disappoint her...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: I'd sometimes serve as her audience when she worked on her graffiti. I gave her all the ideas I could. Like... I'd tell her about all the amazing things I've seen while riding Turbo Twirly up on the clifftops.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: I haven't really hung out with her that many times, but just seeing her so hard at works make me want to work harder too.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: I've heard that she received inspiration from someone, and has become more talkative as a result, even joining some sort of... grand graffiti gang a few years back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! The Dopey Dazzler's become a real big shot in the Graffiti Alliance, while you've become a cornerstone of your tribe's warriors!

choices.text: The two of you have made great strides.

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: As expected, the Dopey Dazzler's been working hard in her field too...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: And here I am, still so far away from becoming that "important warrior of the tribe"... Oh, that's right! I've got to get ready for the next tournament!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right. Let's all do our best, shall we?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: In that case, I'll leave you to it... I've got to continue practicing, sharpening my skills, and readying myself...

choices.text: The two of you are moving up in life!
That's a very "Kachina" line of thought.
Almost like the colors of some delicious food.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, like... coffee lemon cake with mint... Ugh, this analogy's making Paimon hungry.

choices.text: Our task is a bit abstract, but it's interesting all the same.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ehh, is that you, Dopey Dazzler? Looking for potential graffiti spots nearby, huh?

dialogues.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
dialogues.text: Ah, you're here too. Looks like you're really talented, picking the most promising scenery like that...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, well... not quite. So far, we've been pretty "feast or famine" when it comes to inspiration!

choices.text: Were you about to start working your magic here?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, that's true. We haven't seen graffiti in progress yet, have we? Could you show us?

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Don't rush things. There are no suitable cliffs nearby — after all, avant-garde graffiti requires an avant-garde canvas!

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: I just happened to be passing through this area, and I recalled having a picnic here with a friend once, which is why I dropped by this spot again.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: If it wasn't for that friend's encouragement, I might have remained a tongue-tied, ordinary artist. Someone with no head for anything other than graffiti, unable to comprehend even the most basic of avant-garde philosophies.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: And of course, I'd never have met you two.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... Sounds like you're talking about a dear friend who gave you important life advice!

choices.text: Like how Paimon and I travel together, then?

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Well, I wouldn't say we're that close — you're almost joined at the hip, you know!

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: I met her many years ago, I was studying color mixing at the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. It was the unique color scheme of her clothes that immediately drew my eye.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Other people would say that I look like someone whose soul's been torn out of their body when I think about colors and paints, and I didn't have many friends.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: But she thought differently. She believed that my "dopey-ness" was a sign that I was sure about my goals and wasn't concerned about anything else, just like a warrior in training.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: It wasn't any impassioned, encouraging speech, but she motivated me greatly just the same. We haven't kept in contact too much over the years, but I've never forgotten her words.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: She doesn't have any talent for graffiti, but that's fine. She became an awesome warrior all the same — in fact, I believe that someday, the Children of Echoes will all be proud of her...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, that's a new one... So friends who don't hang out often can encourage each other too!

choices.text: All the best to both of you.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Haha, don't you worry about that!

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Danger and unexpected accidents are temporary. She'll be up and over those obstacles for sure!

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: And I won't be standing idle either. There's always room to improve my graffiti skills, and I'm sure a breakthrough's on the horizon once I combine them with my latest thoughts on avant-garde art!

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: I'll paint something massive for her when she returns in triumph. Just watch me!

choices.text: I wish you both luck moving up in life!
Does your friend do graffiti as well?
Mind showing us your masterful artistry?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Kachina, is that you?

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}? Paimon? Well, I sure didn't expect to see you here!

dialogues.speaker: Kachina
dialogues.text: Considering your skills, you must be here on some crazy commission. Something to do with that Spiritway over there, maybe?

choices.text: Our present commission is pretty awesome, yes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Speaking of which, the person who commissioned us is also from the Children of Echoes. Maybe you know each other...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You describe your encounter with "Dopey Dazzler," her views on graffiti, and her invitation for you to study avant-garde thought...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Ah, the Dopey Dazzler. You could call us friends, hehe...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: She doesn't look like a big deal, quite like me, in fact. But if you get her talking, she can go on forever... If you hang out with her a bit more, you might see a... different side to Natlan, I guess?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Did you become friends after she invited you to draw graffiti with her as well?

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Graffiti's one of the reasons we're friends... But I guess it's better to say that it was a happy coincidence?

response.speaker: Kachina

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: I've heard that she received inspiration from someone, and has become more talkative as a result, even joining some sort of... grand graffiti gang a few years back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! The Dopey Dazzler's become a real big shot in the Graffiti Alliance, while you've become a hero here in Natlan!

choices.text: Moving up in life, you two!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Thank you... Uh, no, stop looking at me. I'm not going to cry! I'm just... getting a bit emotional...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: I'm just glad to know that the Dopey Dazzler's been working hard in her own field... Must have been a tough road for her...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: I suppose I could call myself a qualified warrior nowadays... But I'm not sure "famous" is a fitting description...

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Ah, I'd love to have a chat with her the next time we meet.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right. We're all gonna do our best!

response.speaker: Kachina
response.text: Yup, that's right! I'll keep forging ahead. And if you don't mind... Could I continue studying under you once you finish your work with the Dopey Dazzler?

choices.text: The promise you made will come true for sure.
You're absolutely right, Kachina.
Almost like the colors of some delicious food.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, like... coffee lemon cake with mint... Ugh, this analogy's making Paimon hungry.

choices.text: Our task is a bit abstract, but it's interesting all the same.

dialogues.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
dialogues.text: So... You've also come to the Scions of the Canopy's territory... Some pretty nice views around here, wouldn't you say?

dialogues.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
dialogues.text: Standing way up high, you can see all kinds of terrain... The shapes of all kinds of things... will also... look different...

dialogues.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
dialogues.text: Phew... *panting*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dopey Dazzler? We didn't think you'd get here before us! Though, you don't look so good...

choices.text: Need to catch your breath?

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: This is why I envy the tribe's warriors so much, with their endless reserves of stamina... Graffiti is also hard work, but our bodies just can't keep up...

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Sometimes, I can't help but think that Yumkasaurs are really good companions. After all, they can effortlessly navigate even the most steep and rugged terrain. It's a godsend for graffiti artists.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's a good point! With a Yumkasaur to help, travel is a whole lot easier...

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Of course! Though I'm not at all saying that Tepetlisaur companions aren't good enough. After all, a Yumkasaur couldn't even begin to imagine how to do some of the things they can...

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Like helping to excavate critical ores from deep underground, and making paints with some amazing effects... Now that's priceless!

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Plus, looking at things from a much broader perspective, the most important thing about your companion isn't their abilities — I care more about the emotional connection. Who cares about all that utilitarian codswallop?

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Even if climbing mountains and crossing rivers is a bit more tiring for me, so what? There's no way I'd even consider something like... leaving the Children of Echoes and joining the Scions of the Canopy, or anything ridiculous like that.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Ooof... Sorry for throwing all that at you, I must be getting dizzy from exhaustion. Let me take a little break...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon never thought the Dopey Dazzler would be able to get so serious... Well, now we know you're the type of person who cares a lot about their companions and comradery!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon and {NICKNAME} are like that too! When we make friends, we never think, "What can this person do for me?" It all starts with... what would you call it?

choices.text: Compatibility?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, yeah, something like that?

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Speaking of companions... there's a powerful Saurian Hunter among the Scions of the Canopy named Kinich. He is often accompanied by a rather extraordinary companion.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: That companion's coloration is unusually vivid. Were I to use the professional lingo of Fontainian painters... I'd say the saturation levels are really high, and far more deserving of the name "dazzler"!

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: And Kinich himself also has a very avant-garde sense of style... His appearance just screams "natural artist"!

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Shame, though. Lots of members of my Alliance drew graffiti near his usual haunts to get his attention, but he doesn't seem to care at all. Seems like he really isn't into graffiti.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that how the Graffiti Alliance usually recruits new members? Seems like a lot of time and effort...

choices.text: Seems like a compatibility issue.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Yeah, that's right! You can't force it.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Super-strong Saurian Hunters are probably only attracted by other powerful figures, like you two! Once the two of you are famous members of the Graffiti Alliance, maybe then he'll take an interest in graffiti!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That logic's pretty "avant-garde," too. Stuff like this, you'll never know until you try.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So there's no need to rush things!

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Alright, I'll take your advice this time.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: But you guys better work hard so you can accumulate enough inspiration, ASAP!

choices.text: You can't force serendipity.
Serendipity?
Climbing up and down must be tiring.

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Mwahaha, at long last! The almighty dragonlord K'uhul Ajaw has shattered that which bound him, and graces the world with his majestic presence once more!

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Hope you've learned your lesson.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Kinich! We didn't expect to see you here!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Oh... it's you two little... things.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! You little... how are you still so arrogant!?

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Hmph. Forget it. I'll let that slide for now, as I happen to be in a good mood today.

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: I had him locked up before, and just released him, so...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! So you just let him out? No wonder!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Released, shmeleased! I totally was the one who broke free!

dialogues.speaker: Ajaw
dialogues.text: Besides, Kinich, not like you even know what's good for yourself anyway. If these two chumps had an unfortunate accident, couldn't you make a fortune out of saving them?

dialogues.speaker: Kinich
dialogues.text: Enough of your blustering.

choices.text: It's fine. That's just how Ajaw is.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Hmph! Looks like someone is only half-blind.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Are the two of you here because of graffiti?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wha—? Kinich, how'd you know that?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Members of the Graffiti Alliance have been active around here lately. There was some concern they might encounter danger while at work, and so I was commissioned to come look.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Though with you here, there was never a need to worry in the first place.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Hey, that's right! This pasty little pixie doesn't even have the right to draw graffiti, much less get herself in danger!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! Just what're you trying to say?

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: It's a rule of the Scions of the Canopy: Only those who pass the trial have the right to draw graffiti! You've gotta be brave enough to leap from the peaks over there, but do you have the guts?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Isn't that just bungee jumping? Paimon's heard of it, just an extreme sport, nothing special.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Oho, this is no ordinary extreme sport! It's a trial, you see, a trial!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So how's it different then?

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: You don't even know that? Pathetic. Fine, I'm willing to waste some of my precious time helping you be a bit less ignorant.

choices.text: Wow, you'd really do something nice for someone?

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: First, before you start climbing, you've gotta show your bravery by dumping everything but your clothes at the foot of the mountain. That means no ropes, no knives, no wind gliders, no nothing!

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: If you bring anything, even the teeniest doo-dad, it counts as disrespecting the trial and you instantly fail! Once you reach the summit, you've gotta run around it three times, and then...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And then what?

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Then you leap! And then you relax your whole body.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Doesn't that just mean you fall down the mountain!?

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: Naw, you'd be fine! If even an iota of what I said was false, then may I immediately be imprison— HEY! Wait, servant, what're you doing, a—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Kinich, he was just getting to the most important part! Why'd you lock him up?

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: Paimon, we generally call jumping off a high cliff without a rope "suicide."

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: The reason for his earlier confinement was because he attempted to trick members of the Graffiti Alliance into jumping off cliffs.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Argh! That loathsome little lizard! He was up to no good after all! He deserves to get locked up again!

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: My apologies to both of you. In any case, please do pay attention to your safety around here. I still need to patrol a few other areas, so I'll be taking my leave now.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: As for the members of the Graffiti Alliance, don't you worry. I'll handle their safety.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay! Hopefully it won't be too much trouble.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: No trouble at all. It's part of the commission, after all.

response.speaker: Kinich
response.text: As for Ajaw, after his time out is over, I'll let him experience the thrill of ropeless bungee jumping for himself.

choices.text: Where's the real Ajaw and what'd you do with him?
It's fine. I'm not the type to stoop to squabbling with little things like him.

response.speaker: Ajaw
response.text: I'm no "little thing"!

dialogues.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
dialogues.text: Hehe, fancy bumping into the two of you again, and at none other than the finest scenic spot that the People of the Springs has to offer! Not only that, this place is universally recognized as one of the most stunning sights in the whole of southern Natlan.

dialogues.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
dialogues.text: The azure blue of the vast expanses of water, the lush green of the mountain vegetation, intertwined with the intense fiery hues of the phlogiston... Simply breathtaking, and a masterclass intro to color contrast too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dopey Dazzler! Pretty fast on your feet, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No use lecturing us on color theory yet though — we still won't get it...

choices.text: Do you know the People of the Springs well?

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Well, core members of the Graffiti Alliance technically make it their mission to travel to every corner of Natlan, familiarizing themselves with the culture and customs of all the different tribes.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: A while back now, the People of the Springs hired us to spray-paint their watersports gear. It was a very large order, so I had to stay here for quite some time.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: They paid us very well, so to return the favor, I decided it was only fair if I made the design I sprayed onto each and every one of their watersports products totally unique.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: In the end, after two months of slogging away, I'd only finished less than five percent of the total... My hands were so sore they felt like they were about to fall off, and my brain had totally crashed...

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: And to make matters worse, new products were constantly being churned out. If things kept going the way they were, I'd never have been able to finish the job...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A unique design, for every, single, individual, watersports product...!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... there are watersports products everywhere at the People of the Springs — you couldn't even count them if you tried. That goal was totally crazy!

choices.text: Even if you had twenty Dopey Dazzlers on the job, you'd still struggle...

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Yes, well... in the end, we came to realize that. Our clever client from the People of the Springs proposed a more cost-effective solution instead—

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: The new plan was that we would come up with a single batch of graffiti designs, create stencils based on the designs, specify the colors required, and then roughly mark out where they needed to be sprayed.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Then, the clients' own people would spray the designs onto a large batch of watersports equipment themselves — following our instructions, of course.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, that sounds like a great idea! It wouldn't require a lot of manpower, so it'd save heaps of time and effort. Plus, you wouldn't even need to go to the trouble of training them up.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is this also some kind of... avant-garde production philosophy?

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Mmm... Yes, I suppose you could say that! Of course, in an ideal world, it would all be done by hand, but we're not that inflexible.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: If it helps our art reach a wider audience, we shouldn't force ourselves to stick rigidly to the principles of "pure" handicraft.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Anyway, all in all, I'm full of awe and admiration for our friends at the People of the Springs. They think on their feet, and they're always full of ideas...

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: A watersports shop owner named Mualani, who also happens to be one of the tribe's renowned warriors, spent a few days with us learning graffiti.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Overflowing with enthusiasm and talent, that one. It wasn't long at all before she was producing bona-fide artwork to decorate her surfboard with...

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Now I come to think of it, she's the perfect role model for you guys!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: From the sound of it, as long as you have the necessary commitment and the motivation, learning graffiti over a short period of time... isn't completely impossible, then?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, we need to up our game! We'll have to find some good materials and get to grips with this avant-garde mindset, ASAP! Paimon can't wait to start doodling all over her favorite objects too, hehe...

choices.text: Sounds like what we need is a crash course in graffiti.

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Boom, that's what I'm talking about! You're finally coming around...!

response.speaker: "Dopey Dazzler"
response.text: Well, I'll say no more, only this... Open your eyes, clear your minds. Soak up the incredible scenery around you. Look for anything that captures your imagination and inspires creativity, anything — lines, shapes, colors! And with that in mind, sally forth!

choices.text: About time we jazzed up some of our own gear too!
Why would you put that much pressure on yourself...
You must have visited many times before?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: #Aha, if it isn't {NICKNAME} and Paimon! Not looking for some graffiti inspiration near the People of the Springs, by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: If so, you've sure come to the right place. This area of ours is one of the best scenic spots in the whole of southern Natlan!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Mualani! Paimon's feeling even more pumped, now we've run into you!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But how could you tell we were searching for inspiration for our graffiti?

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: Hehe, guides like me tend to keep our ears to the ground...

dialogues.speaker: Mualani
dialogues.text: As it just so happens, some members of the Graffiti Alliance dropped by a while back, and they mentioned that the Dopey Dazzler's been teaching you guys some artistic philosophy.

choices.text: You're well-acquainted with the Graffiti Alliance, then?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: We don't see an awful lot of one another, but we're still old friends!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Everywhere in Natlan, no matter which tribe you go to, there's a huge demand for graffiti. Aside from the walls of buildings, people also regularly decorate items that they use...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Especially the most important things of all, like swim rings, surfboards, beach volleyballs, parasailing gear... Okay, that's probably enough examples... Anyway, when it comes to watersports products, people put a lot of thought into how they look!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Back in the day, when craftsmen made watersports equipment, they'd decorate them with colors and simple patterns based on what they themselves thought looked good.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: But then people began to realize that expert graffiti artists could design swim rings and surfboards with far more dynamic designs and striking colors...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So you hired a certain someone from the Graffiti Alliance... to come up with a unique design for every single swim ring and surfboard in existence?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Hahaha, that's a bit over the top... If someone actually tried spray painting every single one by hand, their hand would probably end up falling off!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: A certain quirky-minded graffiti expert did, for a time, insist on creating a unique design for every individual watersports product. But after a heroic attempt, they realized it was an impossible task.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: So instead, we suggested that the Graffiti Alliance come up with some standardized designs and create special stencils for mass production.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: This way, all you have to do is put on a pair of gloves, place the stencils on top of the items, spray on the paint step by step, leave them somewhere to dry, then apply a layer of wax, and... Tada! Job done!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Th—That's a good point... The People of the Springs is such a huge tribe, who knows how long it would take even just to come up with all the different designs...

choices.text: About your surfboard, Mualani...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Ah, well, my surfboard's one-of-a-kind. After all, it only looks the way it does 'cause I picked up some graffiti skills and painted it myself!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: As both a first-rate guide of the People of the Springs and the owner of a famous watersports shop, my business depends on my ability to stand out from the crowd! And people wouldn't be very impressed if my gear just looked the same as everyone else's, would they?

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Anyway, the main point is this — the only way you'll end up with a design that you're a hundred percent happy with... is if you create it yourself! That way, you can even use your lucky color!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No wonder Paimon's starting to understand why she felt more motivated as soon as she saw you, Mualani.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're... just the type of person who'd figure even the hardest stuff out, as long as you like it!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Honestly, it isn't difficult at all! Graffiti's like... beach volleyball. It's not like traditional painting, all rigid and formal. As long as you can capture roughly what you're aiming for, you'll do just fine.

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: For you two, becoming top graffiti masters shouldn't take much time at all...

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: It's a pity things have been a bit manic at the shop recently, so I've got a bit too much on my plate right now. Once I've gotten things back under control, I'll make some time to come do some graffiti with you!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh! Nice to have your vote of confidence, Mualani!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Let's keep working on it, {NICKNAME}! The sooner we can find some good materials and wrap our heads around Dopey Dazzler's avant-garde philosophy, the better!

choices.text: I'll trust you on this one too, Mualani!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: #Aha! Best of luck, {NICKNAME}, Paimon!

response.speaker: Mualani
response.text: Perhaps someday I'll need you guys to create designs for the watersports products in my shop! We'll give each other "friendly rates" when the time comes, alright?

choices.text: Priority one, graffiti. Priority two, beach volleyball.
Which maestro made the Sharky Surfboard?
So you know the Dopey Dazzler too?
